TECHLENS NETWORK FORENSICS
Guidance on this tool
Understand the capture, choose the right analyzer, and investigate network evidence step by step.

      

      
    

    

      

        
HAR · NETLOG · SAZ · LOG · PCAPNG · ETW EXPORTS
What is Tech Lense Analyzer?
Tech Lense Analyzer is a standalone, browser-based network-forensics workspace for inspecting supported evidence including HAR, Chromium / Microsoft Edge NetLog JSON, Fiddler SAZ, diagnostic LOG, PCAPNG, and decoded ETW XML/CSV exports. The exact fields and analysis depth depend on the source format. It organizes available evidence into requests, domains, headers, cookies, timing, request details, diagnostic indicators and findings so an engineer can move from a capture to a focused investigation.
Important: The tool analyzes the capture you provide. It does not automatically prove root cause. Use the evidence and the “Confirmed / Probable / Not Established” mindset when drawing conclusions.

        
HARHTTP ArchiveBest for request / response investigation
NETLOGedge://net-export JSONBest for browser network-stack events
SAZFiddler session archiveHTTP sessions and captured request/response data

      


      
CURRENT RELEASE · v1.6.5
Current features, supported workflows and limits
Import progress reports actual file bytes read, then separate decode/parse/index stages. Large-file preflight warnings can be cancelled without replacing the current evidence.

        
Three Look & Feel optionsWarm Daylight is the default. Users can switch to Modern Executive or Nostalgia with the theme controls. Theme selection changes the presentation only, not how evidence is parsed.

        
Evidence importImport HAR, Edge/Chromium NetLog JSON, Fiddler SAZ, diagnostic LOG/TXT traces, PCAP/PCAPNG, decoded ETW XML/CSV, cURL or raw HTTP. ZIP/GZ/TGZ paths accept recognized evidence members; unsupported archive content may be skipped. Raw ETL needs conversion first.

        
Multi-file investigationsUse ＋ Add Evidence to append another capture instead of replacing the current case. Review the source-file inventory and preserve provenance when comparing records.

        
Request ExplorerSearch/filter and sort the request grid by resource icon, method, result, process, protocol, host, URL, body size, cache directives, content type, elapsed time, session type, authentication, host IP, response server, cookies, evidence source and initiator. Empty values mean the source did not capture that field.

        
DiagnosticsReview DNS, proxy, authentication, network access, OSI-layer, TLS/certificate and server/HTTP indicators, plus All Findings & Export and Advanced Root Cause Analysis.

        
Correlation and RCACorrelates records by available timestamps, endpoints, request identifiers, statuses/errors and sequence patterns. These are investigative indicators—not proof of causation. Check supporting and counter-evidence.

        
Identify Log & Source InfoSummarizes file type, source inventory, record counts, time range, domains, protocols, HTTP status counts and observed User-Agent or explicit environment fields where present. Missing fields are reported as unavailable rather than guessed.

        
Reports and review actionsCopy Finding, Export Report, Copy review and Export review (.txt) support quick sharing of investigation summaries. Review exported content for secrets and organization-specific identifiers before sending it.

        
Waterfall & Performance (v1.35)Open Waterfall & Performance to review the current Request Explorer result set, duration distribution, p50/p95, failures, slow sessions and phase bars. Rows with real start timestamps are ordered chronologically. Rows without timestamps are clearly unanchored and shown as duration-only; do not infer overlapping execution from them.

        
Timing phase accuracyDNS, connection, TLS, send, wait/TTFB, receive and blocked values are shown only when the imported record has usable non-negative timings. Missing phases are not zero. If phase totals and elapsed duration disagree, the difference is called out rather than silently corrected.

        
WebSocket Messages (best effort)For SAZ archives, the analyzer looks for raw WebSocket message files associated with captured sessions. Recognized text or JSON-line records can be displayed; unknown formats remain raw-only. Binary frames, fragmentation, and every exporter variation are not guaranteed to decode. gRPC payload decoding is not yet implemented.

        
Local processing, progress and file sizeEvidence reading, parsing and indexing run in this browser tab; import does not automatically upload the file. The progress panel separates bytes read from total file size and later parsing/indexing stages. Large files show a pre-import warning; the UI has a 512 MB expanded-data limit, but available browser memory and capture complexity still matter.

      
SAZ caveat: compare imported session count and representative request/response headers, statuses, timestamps and timings against Fiddler Classic/Everywhere. WebSocket messages are decoded best-effort only when matching message files and a recognized text format are present; binary frames and uncommon SAZ variations may not be fully preserved. gRPC entries can be identified, but payload decoding is not implemented.


      

        
01
When should I use HAR?
Use a HAR when you need to inspect web requests and responses: URL, method, status, headers, cookies, request payloads, response information, timing, initiator and waterfall behavior.
  • HTTP 401 / 403 / 407 / 5xx investigation
  • Redirect and authentication flows
  • API request / response troubleshooting
  • Slow requests and waterfall analysis
  • Cookie, header and parameter inspection

        
02
When should I use NetLog?
Use a NetLog when you need lower-level browser network-stack evidence that may not be represented completely in a HAR.
  • DNS / socket / connection investigation
  • Proxy and network-stack troubleshooting
  • TLS / connection sequencing
  • Browser network errors
  • Source IDs and event timelines

        
03
Which file should I collect?
.har → Edge / Chrome DevTools Network export.
.saz → Fiddler Classic / Fiddler Everywhere saved session archive.
.json → Edge edge://net-export / Chromium NetLog dump.
The analyzer detects the structure instead of trusting only the file extension. A JSON file containing log.entries[] is treated as HAR; a JSON file containing the NetLog event structure is treated as NetLog.

      


      
QUICK START
How to use the tool

        
1
Capture the issue
Reproduce the problem while collecting the relevant browser network trace. Keep the capture focused on the scenario you are investigating.

        
2
Export the evidence
For DevTools, export the Network activity as HAR. For browser network-stack diagnostics, collect a NetLog JSON from edge://net-export.

        
3
Open Tech Lense Analyzer
Click Browse & Select Evidence File or drag a file onto the drop zone. After one file is loaded, use ＋ Add Evidence to append related captures. The file is processed locally in your browser.

        
4
Confirm the capture type
Check the source/evidence badges and Identify Log & Source Info summary. Use the reported format and fields actually present; not every format provides HTTP bodies, timings, or machine identity.

        
5
Start broad, then narrow
Review the statistics first, then use Domains, search, status/type filters, Failed, Slow, and the clickable summary cards to focus the Request Explorer.

        
6
Inspect the evidence
Select a request and review Overview, Headers, Params, Request Body, Response, Timing, Waterfall and NetLog Events where available.

      


      
UNDERSTAND THE SCREEN
What each area does

        
StatisticsQuick filters for total requests, 2xx, 3xx, 4xx, 5xx, slow requests and domains.

        
DomainsGroup traffic by host so you can quickly identify Microsoft, identity, API, proxy or third-party endpoints.

        
Request ExplorerThe main investigation table. Search and filter requests, then select a row for detailed inspection.

        
Request InspectorDeep view of the selected request: URL, status, headers, cookies, payload, response, timing and evidence.

        
WaterfallUse timing relationships to identify slow, blocked, delayed or unusually long requests.

        
NetLog EventsFor NetLog captures, inspect available network-stack events and event sequencing.

        
Identify Log & Source InfoAfter importing evidence, open Evidence Info in the right-side navigator or use the in-workspace Evidence Source Info menu to review detected format and observed metadata. It cannot infer a computer/user identity unless that value is explicitly present.

        
Diagnostics and RCAUse the diagnostic category buttons for targeted clues, then compare findings with source records. Heuristic rankings are not a confirmed root cause.

        
Review copy/exportCopy review places summary text on the clipboard where browser permissions allow; Export review saves a plain-text file. Watch for confirmation feedback.

      


      
INVESTIGATION WORKFLOW
A practical engineer workflow
Capture→Validate→Filter→Inspect→Correlate→Conclude
Example: If a sign-in scenario shows a 401, do not immediately label it as “authentication is broken.” Inspect the request headers, response headers, redirect chain, timing and surrounding requests. If NetLog is available, correlate the browser network events before deciding what the evidence establishes.


      
!
Security & privacy
HAR, NetLog, packet captures and ETW exports can contain sensitive information. Depending on how the trace was collected, captures may include cookies, authorization-related data, URLs, query parameters, internal hostnames or other diagnostic information.
  • Use sanitized HAR exports whenever possible.
  • Review captures before sharing them.
  • Do not paste tokens, passwords or secrets into reports.
  • Follow your organization's data-handling requirements.
i
Know the limits
HAR, NetLog, SAZ, LOG, PCAPNG and decoded ETW exports contain different fields. A NetLog is event-based and may not contain HAR-style request/response bodies; PCAPNG and decoded ETW views also depend on their available packets/events and any decryption or decoding performed before import.
  • Missing data is not proof that an event did not happen.
  • Browser-local analysis does not make a sensitive capture safe to share.
  • Use packet traces, application logs, server logs or identity logs when the evidence requires them.


      
QUICK REFERENCE
Capture → Analyze → Report
HAR: Browser DevTools Network → reproduce → export HAR → import here.
Fiddler: Save sessions as a .SAZ archive → import the SAZ file. Standard HTTP sessions are supported; WebSocket payload extraction is best-effort, gRPC payload decoding is not implemented, and perfect binary-body fidelity is not guaranteed. ZIP/TGZ bundles containing recognized evidence files are supported; arbitrary archive contents are skipped.
NetLog: open edge://net-export → reproduce → stop/save capture → import the JSON here.
LOG / PCAPNG / ETW: import supported diagnostic logs, Wireshark captures, or decoded ETW/WPA XML/CSV exports. Convert raw .ETL to a supported export first.

TECH LENSE ANALYZER · LOCAL WORKFLOW
Local Processing & Privacy
Know where evidence is processed and what may leave the browser.

      
    

    

      
Evidence import stays in this browser tab.The standalone analyzer does not automatically upload the selected evidence file during import, parsing or indexing.

      

        
🧭 What happens locally?
Selected files are read and analyzed by the page in your browser. Import progress reports local file reading, then parser and indexing stages. Large captures can use substantial memory; cancel the large-file warning if you are not ready to proceed.

        
🤖 AI Copilot and external providers
If you configure and use an external AI provider, the selected prompt and context sent for that request may be transmitted to that provider. Review the selected context, provider configuration and your organization’s AI/data-handling rules first.

        
🛡️ Sensitive network evidence
HAR, NetLog, SAZ, PCAP/PCAPNG and ETW data may contain cookies, authorization values, URLs, query parameters, request/response bodies, internal hostnames, IP addresses or identity-related metadata. Treat imported and exported evidence as potentially sensitive.

        
📤 Reports and redaction
Copied findings and exported TXT/PDF/report content can include identifiers from the source evidence. PII-safe or redaction features are best-effort, not a guarantee. Inspect and sanitize outputs before sharing them outside the approved support team.

      

      
Important: Browser-local processing does not make a capture safe to share. Follow your organization’s evidence retention, access and privacy requirements. Raw ETL must be converted to a supported decoded export before import.

            ⚡
            Fast Troubleshooting Checklist
          

          
For proxy challenges, inspect HTTP 407 and Proxy-Authenticate. For authentication failures, correlate 401/403, redirects and token acquisition. For upstream/gateway failures, correlate HTTP 5xx with timing and DNS/TLS evidence.
